decisions.reason: As a young product close to the core heat-exchange portfolio in a growing market, sunk engineering and launch effort plus the firm's public commitment make management more likely to continue than to reverse course.

Because this condenser fits the firm's established thermal-systems business and stated move toward efficient solutions, management would tend to justify prior investment by keeping it on the market unless failure became unmistakable.
Its strong overlap with existing capabilities, strategic fit, and absence of clear evidence of persistent failure support continued backing under an escalation-of-commitment logic.
This repair-oriented liner reinforces the firm's lifecycle-service model and installed-base business, so accumulated development effort and customer relevance favor retention.
As a customized product line with several models and visible alignment with core industrial markets, it represents a broader commitment that management is especially likely to sustain.
